newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Feb industrial output rises 1.9 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: German Feb industrial output rises 1.9 pct m/m.

text.p: German industrial production, driven by manufacturing strength and a seasonal rebound in construction, rose 1.9 percent month-over-month in February and 7.1 percent from a year ago, official data showed on Thursday.

The Economics Ministry said construction output climbed 16.6 percent in February after harsh weather dampened the sector's performance the month before. But even without the boost from construction, February's output was up 0.5 percent.

"Particularly the clear recovery in the manufacturing sector -- the core industry sector -- continued the clear upswing of the past few months," the Economics Ministry said, adding that the figures were preliminary.
Most of the month's gain came from eastern Germany, where total output rose 8.1 percent in February. West German output increased 0.9 percent, the ministry said.
Year-on-year, February production rose 12.6 percent in eastern Germany and 5.4 percent in western Germany

Pan-German manufacturing production rose 1.1 percent in February, with the sector showing particular strength in eastern Germany, where manufacturing output rose 4.5 percent. In western Germany, manufacturing output edged up 0.8 percent compared to January's total.
West German construction rose 11.4 percent month-on-month, and eastern German construction climbed 31.2 percent, the ministry said.
Energy production showed the greatest decline month-on-month, falling 7.1 percent as cold snap in January gave way to warmer temperatures in February.
